title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock V
spaceBreakdown:
- three vectors f, l, s of size k+1 each (rolling, rebuilt per day but reused via swap) → O(k)
- per-day temporaries nf, nl, ns of size k+1 → O(k)
- no recursion
- not counted: input prices
approach: Track three states per number of completed transactions: free, holding a long position, holding a short position. Each day you either start a transaction (pay/receive the price), close one (collect the price), or do nothing. Since each completed transaction consumes one of the k slots, iterating days × k with rolling arrays gives O(n·k), which fits n ≤ 10^3, k ≤ n/2 easily.
hints: At any moment you are either idle, mid-way through a buy-then-sell, or mid-way through a sell-then-buy-back - and each finished deal eats one of your k chances. How would you describe the best outcome using only "days so far, deals finished, and current position"?

Use DP with three states per transaction count (free / long / short). On prices=[1,7,9,8,2], k=2: after day 2 (price 9), free-with-1-deal becomes 8 (buy 1, sell 9), and short-with-1-deal becomes 15 (sell 7, pending buy-back).

free[j] = best profit idle with j deals done
long[j] = holding bought stock, j deals done
short[j] = holding sold stock, j deals done
for each price p:
    for j in 0..k:
        newFree[j] = max(free[j], long[j]+p, short[j]-p)   # close a deal (j+1 slot used via index shift)
        newLong[j] = max(long[j], free[j]-p)
        newShort[j] = max(short[j], free[j]+p)
return free[k]

**Overflow** - k = 500 deals each earning up to ~10^9 gives ~5×10^11 total.
`Input: prices = [1,1000000000,1,1000000000], k = 2` → `Expected: 1999999998`
⚠️ Bug: storing dp values in int → overflows past 2^31−1, returns a wrapped negative value.

**All equal prices** - no deal can profit, answer is 0.
`Input: prices = [5,5,5,5], k = 2` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: forcing exactly k deals instead of at most k → returns 0 only by luck here, but on [5,5,4,4] it would return −2 instead of 2.

**Strictly decreasing** - only short selling helps.
`Input: prices = [9,7,5,3], k = 1` → `Expected: 6`
⚠️ Bug: only modeling normal buy/sell transactions → returns 0.

**Smallest input** - n = 2, one day pair only.
`Input: prices = [3,10], k = 1` → `Expected: 7`
⚠️ Bug: allowing buy and sell on the same day or off-by-one in the day loop → returns 13 (3+10) instead of 7.

followUps.q: What if k is unlimited (at most n/2 transactions anyway)?
followUps.a: The k dimension collapses; you can also show the optimal solution only trades on local extrema, giving an O(n) time, O(1) space greedy over peaks and valleys, handling both long and short directions.

followUps.q: What if a fee f is charged per completed transaction?
followUps.a: Subtract f from the profit when closing a deal in the free-state transition; the same O(n·k) state machine works unchanged, and the unlimited-k variant becomes the classic fee-greedy with O(n) time.

followUps.q: What if you must process prices as a stream and cannot store them all?
followUps.a: Keep only the rolling arrays over k states (O(k) memory) and update them as each price arrives - the DP is already streaming-friendly, so memory drops from O(n·k) to O(k) with the same O(n·k) time.
